pos.personaBrief: Flamengo pressed without the ball and then dominated possession (Goal 2019), with a touch-based 6-2 over Palmeiras; it did not cede the ball to counter.

pro.personaBrief: Coutinho wanted the ball recycled back and restarted from the other side, not hoofed, but also fast finishing after winning it and rehearsed long balls like Andrade to Nunes.

est.personaBrief: Sector marking, overlapping fullbacks and polivalence suggest a structured but fluid side with Zico linking play behind the forwards.

lar.personaBrief: Overlapping fullbacks and wide forwards Tita and Junior Cesar gave width, but Zico and Carpegiani central creators were the core.

blo.personaBrief: Coutinho wanted compact teams with high marking lines, pressing from the start and the forwards helping in marking (statedView 1976, Trivela, Lance 6-2).

mar.personaBrief: The only marking term credited to Coutinho is marcacao por setor, a zonal idea, with no evidence of dedicated man-markers.

pla.personaBrief: Coutinho imposed a proactive model of his own with daily drills, though he did show the opponent's scheme before the final.

res.personaBrief: An offensive, massacre-the-opponent team that attacked to win; it played to win rather than settle, and valued the show.

sis.personaBrief: Total participation for everyone including the forward who must help mark, but with Zico as the free star inside a drilled system.

jog.personaBrief: A technical team of Zico, Junior and Adilio with passing and possession, though Coutinho used Cooper-style physical prep and wanted intensity.

bas.personaBrief: Coutinho mixed the club's own youngsters (Zico, Junior, Adilio, Andrade, Tita) with veterans like Carpegiani and Raul; the title was won with homegrown core.

lid.personaBrief: Methodical, professional coach with discipline and studied preparation, but a harmonious group where Zico led without ego and Bosco shielded players.
